s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive swelling of the forearm with a firm, non-tender mass and cortical bone irregularity
salient_findings: Progressively enlarging swelling on the posterior ulnar aspect of the forearm
Firm, non-tender 4 × 5 cm mass in the subcutaneous tissues
Cortical irregularity of the adjacent ulna on radiographs
Mass arising from the bone and extending into the soft tissues on MRI
key_facts: No family history of similar lesions
Normal neurovascular examination of the hand
Soft-tissue swelling with cortical irregularity on radiographs
Mass isointense to muscle on T1-weighted MRI
Cortical bone lysis with medullary involvement

shortlist.label: Osteosarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Aggressive bone lesion with cortical bone lysis and medullary involvement, consistent with osteosarcoma

shortlist.label: Ewing's sarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Bone lesion with soft-tissue extension and marked enhancement after gadolinium administration, consistent with Ewing's sarcoma

shortlist.label: Adamantinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Cortical bone irregularity and medullary involvement, with a firm, non-tender mass, consistent with adamantinoma

shortlist.label: Giant cell tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Bone lesion with cortical bone lysis and soft-tissue extension, although less common in this age group

shortlist.label: Osteoblastoma
shortlist.why_kept: Bone lesion with cortical bone irregularity and medullary involvement, although typically smaller than the described mass

raw.rationale: The presence of cortical bone lysis with medullary involvement and a mass that is isointense to muscle on T1-weighted images and heterogeneous hyperintense on T2-weighted images with marked enhancement after gadolinium administration are consistent with osteosarcoma, a primary malignant bone tumor.

rejected.label: Ewing's sarcoma
rejected.why: While Ewing's sarcoma can also present with bone destruction and soft tissue mass, it typically occurs in younger patients and has a more uniform appearance on MRI.

rejected.label: Adamantinoma
rejected.why: Adamantinoma is a rare bone tumor that typically occurs in the tibia and has a distinct appearance on radiographs and MRI, which does not match the description provided.

rejected.label: Giant cell tumor
rejected.why: Giant cell tumor is a benign bone tumor that typically occurs in adults after epiphyseal closure and has a characteristic 'soap bubble' appearance on radiographs, which is not described in this case.

rejected.label: Osteoblastoma
rejected.why: Osteoblastoma is a rare benign bone tumor that typically occurs in the spine or long bones and has a distinct appearance on radiographs and MRI, which does not match the description provided.
